Krátký update k diktování. Serverová část je skoro hotová, engine běží jako samostatný proces a každá nahrávka zůstává na disku, dokud se text nevloží. Na desktopu s NixOS a niri vkládání funguje v terminálu Ghostty i v prohlížeči Helium. Jediný problém jsou aplikace postavené na frameworku Electron, které občas potřebují krátkou pauzu, než se text vloží. Příště zkusím notebook přes Tailscale. Pokud je spojení přímé, zpoždění by mělo být skoro stejné jako na desktopu. Všechno to zítra sepíšu a v pondělí můžeme probrat slovník.

Ahoj Petře, díky za rychlou odpověď. Návrh jsem si přečetl o víkendu a celkově mi dává smysl. Největší starost mám s harmonogramem. Přesunout všechno na nový cluster najednou mi přijde riskantní, hlavně když se blíží svátky. Nešlo by to rozdělit na dvě fáze? Nejdřív interní nástroje, na kterých nikdo mimo tým nezávisí, a potom služby pro zákazníky, až budeme mít jistotu, že funguje monitoring. Klidně si můžeme zavolat ve středu nebo ve čtvrtek odpoledne, to mám skoro volno. Měj se hezky a pozdravuj ostatní.

Poznámky k dnešnímu incidentu. Ráno začaly v nástroji Grafana chodit alerty pro API gateway. Pody se restartovaly ve smyčce a kubectl ukázal, že je systém zabíjí kvůli nedostatku paměti. Ukázalo se, že nová verze chartu pro Helm zahodila nastavení limitu paměti. Vrátili jsme to přes Argo CD a služba se během pár minut vzpamatovala. Úkoly na příště: přidat do pipeline kontrolu vygenerovaných manifestů, přesunout prahy alertů do pravidel pro Prometheus vedle chartu a napsat krátký návod pro toho, kdo bude mít příště pohotovost. Tikety založím po obědě.

Quick update on the dictation work. The server side is mostly done: the engine runs as a separate process, and every recording stays on disk until its text has been delivered. I tested it on the desktop with NixOS and niri, and pasting works in Ghostty, Helium and VS Code. The only problem is the Electron apps, which sometimes need a short delay before the paste goes through. Next I want to try the laptop over Tailscale. If the connection is direct, the latency should be close to the desktop. If it falls back to a relay, we'll see a few hundred milliseconds more, which is still fine for dictation. I'll write everything up in the decisions document tomorrow, and then we can talk about the dictionary on Monday.

Okay, here's what I want you to do. Look at the clipboard code in the Wayland crate and find out why the restore sometimes runs before the paste has finished. I suspect the timer starts when we send the key event, not when the compositor has actually processed it. niri handles requests in order on one connection, so a sync after the virtual keyboard events should be enough. Please don't change the public types, and keep the new tests in the end to end crate. When you're done, run nextest on the whole workspace, and then open a pull request on GitHub with a short description. If anything is unclear, ask me before you start, not halfway through.

Notes from this morning's incident. Early in the morning the Grafana alerts started firing for the API gateway. The pods were restarting in a loop, and kubectl showed them being killed for running out of memory. It turned out that the new release of the Helm chart had dropped the memory limit override, so the default limit was far too small. We rolled back with Argo CD, and the service recovered within a few minutes. Follow-ups: add a check to the pipeline that compares the rendered manifests, move the alert thresholds into Prometheus rules that live next to the chart, and write a short runbook, so whoever is on call next time doesn't have to dig through the history. I'll create the tickets after lunch.

Hi Martin, thanks for getting back to me so quickly. I had a look at the proposal over the weekend, and I think it makes sense overall. My main concern is the timeline. Moving everything to the new cluster in one go feels risky, especially with the holidays coming up. Could we split it into two phases instead? First the internal tools, which nobody outside the team depends on, and then the customer facing services, once we're confident that the monitoring works. I'm happy to join a call later this week if that's easier. Wednesday and Thursday afternoons are mostly free for me. Best regards, and say hi to the team.

Note to self about the desktop setup. The localwhisper service has to stay installed until psst has been running for a week without problems. After that, disable the service but keep the package, so rolling back is a single rebuild. Home Manager owns the user service for the daemon, and the server runs as a system service with its own state directory. Remember to change the gaming mode script, so it unloads the model through the server instead of stopping the whole service. And check that Noctalia still records the clipboard history after the switch, because the restore logic changes who owns the selection. That's it for now.
